title: The lore update: new rarity tiers, a true Synthblade, and Hallowmere in its place
items: Gear rarity now follows the world's canon: Base (silver), Uncommon (blue), Rare (purple), Legendary (gold) and Exalted (orange). Your old gear keeps its place on the ladder: Issued is now Base, Forged Uncommon, Tempered Rare, Relic Legendary, Sovereign Exalted.
Effect slots: Rare gear has 1, Legendary 2, Exalted 3. For now Cores fill them; Base and Uncommon gear has none. Any Cores already installed in your gear stay right where they are.
Cores no longer raise an item's rarity, and Power counts each item's own rarity. Every Core keeps its effect.
Exalted gear will also grant a buff while equipped. That buff isn't designed yet, so its line reads as a placeholder.

The Synthblade is rebuilt to match the concept art: a real steel longsword with a channel cut along its one synth edge. In a fight the edge Awakens and a contained red barrier fills the channel. Out of combat it settles Dormant: the channel goes dark and it is simply a sword. Its shape never changes.
Defeat no longer implies coming back from the dead. You are Defeated, and the game resumes from your last synchronization point with everything kept.

Hallowmere is now the capital of a much larger Ninth Ward, and these streets are a few of its sites. "The Rot" is what the street calls the abominations, and that they were people once is only what some believe.

Placeholder titles are gone from item names: no more Kings, Saints or Old Kingdom. Your existing items are renamed to match (for example Vael's Hearthplate, Ossery's Verdict). Kade is still the default name, and you can rename your Warden as before.

title: The skill tree, rebuilt: a glowing constellation of Blade, Bulwark and Circuit
items: A new Skills screen [K] / SKILLS: all three branches grow out of the Warden's Oath as one glowing circuit-constellation. Blade burns red, Bulwark steel, Circuit teal.
Every perk is a forged hex node with its own icon and rank segments around it. You can tell at a glance what is locked, open, ready to learn (it pulses), owned, or mastered (solid and glowing).
Traces between perks light up as you invest, and the tier gates show exactly how many points open the next perk. When a new tier opens, a charge of light runs down the line to it.
Select any perk to see what it does, your rank, the exact number now and at the next rank, what it needs, what it costs and what it leads to.

Learn a perk by holding the button (it fills up), or tap the perk again and press Confirm. Unlocking it bursts the node with sparks, flashes the branch colour and sounds a new chime. Mastering a perk adds a bright extra note.
Your skill points sit big and gold at the top, with how far you have gone in each branch. Branch tabs zoom the view in on Blade, Bulwark or Circuit, and arrow keys plus Enter work on a keyboard.
Respec at the Forge: unlearn every perk and get every point back for 15 scrap per point (it asks for a confirm tap).
Built for phones too: the whole tree fits a landscape phone, nothing needs hover, and the Learn button always stays on screen. Your saves carry over untouched.

title: The Armory, rebuilt: see your Warden, compare everything, manage your pack
items: A new Armory screen [I] / GEAR: your Warden stands in the middle in his current gear, turning slowly (drag to spin him), with all six slots around him. His cape, visor and the light at his feet take on the tier of what you wear.
Every item has its own forged icon (Synthblades, helms, cuirasses, gauntlets, greaves, mantles and Cores) framed in its tier colour: Issued, Forged, Tempered, Relic, Sovereign.

Inspect any item to see its stats, Temper level (+0 to +10), installed Cores and empty sockets. Gear you are not wearing shows a side-by-side compare with green and red changes to your damage, armor, health, crit and more.
Filter the pack by slot or Cores and by tier, and sort by newest, rarity, power or slot. New pickups are marked NEW, and a green arrow flags gear stronger than what you wear.
Equip in two taps or clicks: select an item, then tap it again (or press Equip). Tap a worn slot to inspect it and see only gear for that slot.
Lock items to protect them from salvage. Salvaging asks for a confirm tap, and one button clears out every unlocked Issued item at once.
A full stat sheet and your Power rating sit under the Warden, and the Forge & Cores button takes you straight to tempering when you stand at the Forge.
Built for phones too: everything fits a landscape phone screen and nothing needs hover. Your saves carry over automatically.

title: Saving you can trust: 3 slots, autosave, export and import
items: Three save slots. The title screen shows each Warden's name, level, verdict, story progress, where you are, play time and when you last saved. Play, export or delete from there (deleting takes a second tap).
Continue always picks up your most recent Warden, right where you stood, facing the way you faced.

Autosave on everything that matters: picking up loot, equipping, salvaging, tempering, installing or breaking Cores, learning a perk, levelling up, your verdict, each street cleared, the Bellwright, entering a new district, plus every 15 seconds and whenever you switch apps, lock your phone or close the tab.
Loot still lying in the street is saved too, so a reload never eats a Sovereign drop.
Save now from the pause menu, with your slot, play time and last-save time. A small SAVED mark under your health bar confirms each save.
Export your Warden as a save code or a file, and import it on any device (or after clearing browser data) from the title screen. Damaged or cut-off codes are caught before anything is overwritten.
Your 0.4 Warden moves into slot 1 automatically with all gear, Temper, Cores, perks, verdict and progress intact. The old save is kept as a backup.
Each slot keeps a backup of its previous save, so a corrupted write rolls back instead of losing your Warden.

title: Graphics pass: the Synthblade, the Warden and the Rot
items: The Synthblade is a real longsword now: dark faceted steel spine with a fuller, swept crossguard, wrapped grip and a gem pommel. Its single synth edge burns with a flowing, flickering energy shader, crackling lightning forks off it, and it sheds red mist and embers while casting red light on your armor and the street.
Swing trails are tapered, smoothed arcs that burn hot at the edge and fade fast, even at low frame rates.

The Warden is rebuilt: smooth black helm with a glowing red T-visor and cables running into the backplate, layered pauldrons, ridged breastplate, gorget, gauntlets, greaves, belt and pouches, all in scuffed metal that catches the light.
His tattered cape is real cloth now. It trails when you run, whips through rolls and lifts in the wind. Stand still out of combat and he plants the blade point-down, hands on the grip.
Walking and running carry weight (hip sway, counter-twist, leaning into turns), and attacks step into the cut.

The Rot looks wrong in a new way: lumpy, mottled flesh, exposed ribs, a cleaver grafted into a Husk's arm, Skitters with clacking mandibles and jointed legs, and a Bile Spitter with a lamprey mouth. Jaws gape before they strike. Dead abominations burn away in a teal-edged dissolve.

The Bellwright is a hunched bell-ringer now: a cracked bronze bell worn as a head with eyes glowing under the rim, organ-pipe chimneys on its hump, a spiked iron clapper for a hammer and a chain of small bells.
Townsfolk wear real cloaks and hoods. The gaoler carries his lantern and keys, and the watchman has a kettle helm and a halberd.
Phones get lighter models, fewer lightning arcs and fewer particles. Draw calls are about the same as before.

title: Mobile controls: Warden on your phone
items: Play on phones and tablets in landscape. Touch controls only appear on touch devices; keyboard and mouse are unchanged.
Floating left thumbstick: it appears wherever you put your thumb. Push it to the edge to sprint, ease off to walk.
Drag anywhere on the right side to look around. A quick tap there is a light strike.
Thumb buttons: STRIKE (hold to keep the combo going), HEAVY, ROLL, LOCK and STIM. OVERLOAD appears once you learn it, and a glowing FORGE / SEARCH button appears when there is something to use.
GEAR, SKILLS and pause buttons in the top corner. Every menu (naming, judgment, Armory, Forge, Skills, What's new) fits small landscape screens and scrolls.
Phones start at a lighter render scale with quarter-resolution bloom, lighter shadows and less rain, and the game still drops resolution on its own if it struggles.
Hold the phone upright and the game pauses and asks you to turn it sideways. Sound starts on your first tap, including on iPhone.
The objective no longer covers your name on smaller screens, and the HUD respects notches and rounded corners.

title: Combat feel: Perfect Dodge and the last blow
items: Perfect Dodge: roll through an attack at the last instant and the Rot slows to a crawl around you. Strike while your blade burns for a guaranteed critical Riposte (+50% damage), with stamina and Charge refunded.
The last abomination of a fight now falls in slow motion with a deep toll, a lens punch-in and a red shockwave. Felling the Bellwright gets a longer, heavier moment.
Heavy strikes have real weight: the Warden sinks and draws back as the synth edge charges and flares, then throws the whole body into the cut.
Abominations flinch, twist and buckle when your blade lands, so every hit reads.
Snappier controls: dodge out of any wind-up (half the stamina back) or straight out of a finished swing. The blade trail now only streaks during the actual cut.

title: The first night in the Ninth Ward
items: WARDEN replaces Ebbmarrow as the main game. Ebbmarrow stays playable at /arcade/.
Name your Warden and pass your first judgment. Your verdict gives you a trait: Dread, Measure or Inquest.
Third-person synthblade combat: three-hit light combo, heavy strikes, dodge rolls, lock-on, hitstop and blade trails.
Hallowmere's Ninth Ward: Lantern Street, Statute Plaza, Cutpurse Alley and the Grave Gate, in endless rain and fog.
Abominations of the Rot: Hollowed Husks, Skitters, Bile Spitters and the Bellwright.
Gear in five rarity tiers (Issued, Forged, Tempered, Relic, Sovereign). Temper it at the Forge with scrap.
Cores: slot chips into gear for new effects. Every Core raises the item a rarity tier.
Three skill branches (Blade, Bulwark, Circuit) with 15 perks, including the Overload shock nova.
Progress saves automatically in your browser.
